accepted.s:
The International Date Line, in its approximate course, is associated with which of the following?
1. It runs roughly along the 180° meridian.
2. It passes through the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
3. It extends conceptually from the North Pole to the South Pole.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The International Date Line is an imaginary pole-to-pole line, approximately following 180° longitude through the Pacific Ocean. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Use the statement-combination method and verify the line’s location, extent and nature.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A traveller crosses the International Date Line from the American side towards Asia. What is the immediate calendar adjustment?
o: No change is made to the date
The clock is set back by exactly two hours
accepted.x: When the International Date Line is crossed westward from America towards Asia, one calendar day is skipped or added to the date.
accepted.tq: Apply the eastward-westward crossing rule rather than relying only on the direction of clock movement.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s: When the International Date Line is crossed eastward from Asia towards America, which of the following occurs?
o: The date remains unchanged until midnight
accepted.x: Crossing the International Date Line eastward causes the calendar date to go back by one day; consequently, one day is repeated.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the opposite date adjustments for eastward and westward crossings.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The International Date Line deviates from the 180° meridian primarily in order to
o: coincide with the Prime Meridian in the Southern Hemisphere
pass through the largest ocean currents
follow the Equator throughout its course
avoid dividing island groups and countries into different dates
accepted.x: The line zigzags around land areas and island groups so that parts of the same country or group are generally kept on the same calendar date.
accepted.tq: Identify the purpose behind a geographical deviation instead of memorising only its approximate longitude.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs represents neighbouring places on opposite sides of the International Date Line?
accepted.x: Big Diomede belongs to Russia and Little Diomede belongs to the United States; they lie close to each other in the Bering Strait but on different calendar dates.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive geographical pair with the date-line relationship.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The International Date Line passes through the Bering Strait.
2. It is a perfectly straight line following 180° longitude without any deviation.
3. It makes deviations around the Aleutian Islands and some Pacific island groups.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The line passes through or near the Bering Strait and deviates around the Aleutians and Pacific islands. It is not a perfectly straight line.
accepted.tq: Find the false absolute statement; geographical lines commonly have practical deviations.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Pacific islands and the International Date Line is correct?
o: Samoa moved to the American side of the line in 2011.
Samoa moved to the Asian side of the line in 2011.
Fiji abolished its standard time after crossing the line.
Kiribati moved permanently to the Greenwich side of the line in 2011.
accepted.x: Samoa shifted to the Asian side of the International Date Line in 2011, thereby changing its calendar relationship with nearby countries.
accepted.tq: Use the year-and-event association to distinguish a specific date-line adjustment.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following locations is among the first to experience a new calendar day?
accepted.x: Kiribati’s Line Islands use UTC+14 and are among the first inhabited places to enter a new day.
accepted.tq: Recall the extreme positive UTC offset associated with the earliest new day.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Prime Meridian passes through the Royal Observatory at Greenwich and was adopted at the International Meridian Conference held in
accepted.x: The Greenwich Prime Meridian was adopted internationally at the International Meridian Conference in 1884.
accepted.tq: Use the precise year associated with the establishment of the internationally accepted meridian.
accepted.sec: International Date Line - ocean, strait, crossing rule, deviations, neighbours  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the theoretical division of the Earth into time zones?
accepted.x: The theoretical system divides 360° of longitude into 24 time zones, each 15° wide.
accepted.tq: Relate the total circumference of longitude to the number and width of theoretical zones.
accepted.sec: Time zones - number, countries with most zones, cities sharing clock time  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which country has the greatest number of time zones when its overseas territories are included?
accepted.x: France has 12 time zones when its overseas territories are included, while Russia has 11.
accepted.tq: Watch for the qualification ‘including overseas territories’ in country-comparison questions.
accepted.sec: Time zones - number, countries with most zones, cities sharing clock time  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following countries uses a single time zone despite its considerable east-west extent?
accepted.x: China uses one official time zone throughout the country despite its large longitudinal span.
accepted.tq: Use the exception to the expected relationship between longitudinal width and number of time zones.
accepted.sec: Time zones - number, countries with most zones, cities sharing clock time  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following cities has the same clock time as Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai?
accepted.x: Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and Colombo observe UTC+5:30. Nepal uses UTC+5:45 and therefore does not have the same clock time.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure UTC+5:30 pair and distinguish it from nearby quarter-hour offsets.
accepted.sec: Time zones - number, countries with most zones, cities sharing clock time  [other exams]

accepted.s: Nepal’s standard time differs from Indian Standard Time because Nepal observes
accepted.x: Nepal observes UTC+5:45, whereas Indian Standard Time is UTC+5:30, creating a 15-minute difference.
accepted.tq: Test the small quarter-hour offset against the more familiar half-hour standard time.
accepted.sec: Time zones - number, countries with most zones, cities sharing clock time  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains why the Sun rises nearly two hours earlier in Arunachal Pradesh than in western Gujarat?
o: Gujarat has a colder climate than Arunachal Pradesh.
The Earth rotates faster over Arunachal Pradesh.
Arunachal Pradesh lies considerably farther east in longitude than Gujarat.
Arunachal Pradesh is at a higher altitude than Gujarat everywhere.
accepted.x: The nearly two-hour difference in sunrise is primarily due to the large east-west longitudinal extent between Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Identify longitude as the controlling factor in local-time differences rather than climate or altitude.
accepted.sec: Local time gap across India (Arunachal vs Gujarat)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes GMT from UTC?
o: UTC is the local time of the Royal Observatory and GMT is a country-specific standard.
GMT is mean solar time at Greenwich, whereas UTC is maintained using atomic clocks and adjusted with leap seconds.
GMT is based on atomic clocks, whereas UTC is based only on solar observation.
Both GMT and UTC are determined exclusively by the Moon’s revolution.
accepted.x: GMT denotes mean solar time at Greenwich. UTC is the modern world time standard maintained by atomic caesium clocks and adjusted by leap seconds.
accepted.tq: Split the options by the underlying basis—solar observation versus atomic timekeeping.
accepted.sec: GMT/UTC - Greenwich, atomic basis, natural vs conventional units  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a conventional unit of time rather than a natural unit arising directly from astronomical motion?
accepted.x: A day is related to Earth’s rotation, a month to the Moon’s revolution and a year to Earth’s revolution. A week is a conventional unit.
accepted.tq: Separate astronomical natural cycles from socially constructed time divisions.
accepted.sec: GMT/UTC - Greenwich, atomic basis, natural vs conventional units  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Day — rotation of the Earth
2. Month — revolution of the Moon
3. Year — revolution of the Earth
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: A day, month and year are natural time units linked respectively with Earth’s rotation, the Moon’s revolution and Earth’s revolution.
accepted.tq: Verify each unit against its corresponding astronomical motion before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: GMT/UTC - Greenwich, atomic basis, natural vs conventional units  [other exams]

accepted.s: Daylight Saving Time generally involves which of the following practices?
o: Setting clocks back by two hours at the beginning of summer
Changing the calendar date every summer solstice
Advancing clocks by one hour permanently throughout the year
Advancing clocks by about one hour in summer and setting them back in autumn
accepted.x: In many mid- and high-latitude countries, clocks are advanced by about one hour during summer to extend evening daylight and are set back in autumn.
accepted.tq: Recall the seasonal forward-and-backward clock adjustment rather than a permanent time-zone change.
accepted.sec: Daylight saving time concept  [GK]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Daylight Saving Time is correct?
o: It is observed uniformly by every country in the world.
India currently uses it as its national time system.
It changes the longitude of the Prime Meridian.
It is mainly intended to use more evening daylight in summer.
accepted.x: Daylight Saving Time is intended to make better use of available evening daylight in summer. India does not use DST as a national system.
accepted.tq: Reject universal and absolute claims; identify the practical purpose of the measure.
accepted.sec: Daylight saving time concept  [GK]

accepted.s: The Tropic of Cancer is located at approximately
accepted.x: The Tropic of Cancer lies at approximately 23°26′N, commonly rounded to 23.5°N.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the tropical latitude from the polar circle and the Equator.
accepted.sec: Tropic of Cancer - Indian states, nearby cities, meeting point with the standard meridian  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Andhra Pradesh and the Tropic of Cancer?
o: The Tropic of Cancer forms Andhra Pradesh’s northern boundary.
Andhra Pradesh is crossed by the Tropic of Cancer in its northern part.
Andhra Pradesh lies wholly south of the Tropic of Cancer.
Andhra Pradesh lies wholly north of the Tropic of Cancer.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh lies wholly south of the Tropic of Cancer.
accepted.tq: Apply the north-south position of the state rather than confusing it with states through which the parallel passes.
accepted.sec: Tropic of Cancer - Indian states, nearby cities, meeting point with the standard meridian  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following cities is associated with the Indian stretch of the Tropic of Cancer as a city on or near it?
accepted.x: Agartala is one of the Indian cities situated on or near the Tropic of Cancer. The other listed cities are not identified with this parallel in the given context.
accepted.tq: Use a nearby-city association while eliminating cities located well away from the tropical parallel.
accepted.sec: Tropic of Cancer - Indian states, nearby cities, meeting point with the standard meridian  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The orbit of the Earth around the Sun is described as
accepted.x: Earth follows an elliptical orbit around the Sun.
accepted.tq: Recall the standard geometric description of Earth’s orbital path.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Why does a leap year generally occur once in every four years?
o: The Moon completes an extra revolution every four years.
The Earth rotates four times more slowly every fourth year.
The Sun’s apparent path shifts by one complete month every four years.
Earth’s revolution takes approximately an additional quarter of a day beyond 365 days each year.
accepted.x: The revolution period is about 365¼ days. The accumulated quarter-days are adjusted by adding 29 February approximately once every four years.
accepted.tq: Connect the numerical fraction in the orbital period with the calendar correction.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Date/Event)
a. 21 March
b. 21 June
c. 23 September
d. 22 December
List-II (Sun overhead)
i. Tropic of Capricorn
ii. Equator
iii. Tropic of Cancer
iv. Equator

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: On 21 March the Sun is overhead at the Equator; on 21 June at the Tropic of Cancer; on 23 September at the Equator; and on 22 December at the Tropic of Capricorn.
accepted.tq: Start from the solstice pair and then place the two equinoxes at the Equator.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: On 21 June, which one of the following conditions is associated with the Northern Hemisphere?
o: Sun overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn
accepted.x: 21 June is the Northern Hemisphere’s summer solstice. The Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer, producing the longest day and summer conditions there.
accepted.tq: Link the date, overhead latitude and seasonal effect in the relevant hemisphere.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following dates is associated with the winter solstice in the Northern Hemisphere?
accepted.x: The Northern Hemisphere experiences its winter solstice on 22 December, when the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn.
accepted.tq: Use the solstice-equinox calendar sequence to identify the winter date.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. During the equinoxes, day and night are approximately equal everywhere.
2. The equator experiences approximately 12-hour days throughout the year.
3. The poles experience six months of daylight and six months of darkness.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The equinoxes bring approximately equal day and night worldwide. The equator has nearly 12-hour days throughout the year, while the poles experience roughly six months of day and six months of night.
accepted.tq: Combine three day-length facts across different latitudes and seasons.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The seasons on Earth are primarily caused by
o: the tilt of Earth’s axis together with its revolution around the Sun
the elliptical shape of the Moon’s orbit
the changing distance between Earth and the Moon
the daily rotation of Earth alone
accepted.x: Seasons result mainly from the tilt of Earth’s axis combined with Earth’s revolution around the Sun, which changes the angle and duration of solar illumination.
accepted.tq: Identify the combined cause rather than selecting a single-motion explanation.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: During the summer season in the Southern Hemisphere, which pole is tilted towards the Sun?
accepted.x: During southern summer, the South Pole is tilted towards the Sun, producing longer days and summer conditions in the Southern Hemisphere.
accepted.tq: Relate the hemisphere experiencing summer to the direction of axial tilt.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order within a year:
A. Winter solstice
B. Vernal equinox
C. Summer solstice
D. Autumnal equinox
accepted.x: The sequence is vernal equinox around 21 March, summer solstice around 21 June, autumnal equinox around 22/23 September, and winter solstice around 22 December.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence using the four annual astronomical markers.
accepted.sec: Revolution effects - solstices, equinoxes, seasons, day length  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
